name: NewDeductions
judgment_calls: Order of operations in §164(b)(6)(B)/(7): textOrder (reduce and floor the $40,400 amount, then halve for a separate return) is best supported by the words; halve-first readings give gain $0 or $2,835
Baseline taken as the better joint return (itemized, $134,973.50); against joint-standard the gain is $6,282.50
Mortgage interest treated as fully deductible by the spouse who paid it (§163 not in list)
Each spouse deducts only tax that spouse paid; no community property
2026 brackets and standard deduction taken as supplied, not derived
§164(b)(6) applied to 2026 despite the '2018 through 2025' heading, because the operative text and (7)(A)(ii) cover 2026
silences: (7) halves only the threshold for separate returns; silent on halving the $40,400 or the $10,000 floor before the reduction
No instruction to combine spouses' MAGI on separate returns
No rule in §164 on which spouse deducts jointly assessed tax
§68 and AMT outside the list, not encoded
